x: Best performance of the day came from Andy Lloyd, who front ran the 1500 and left everybody for dead as he stretched out a very high class field. Marcello made an unbelieveable breakthrough in the chase and was rewarded by being asked to run the 5000, where he finished a brave 6th.
The clearing up was left until the next day, Sunday morning, and Marcello led the way by washing and hoovering all the floors and Gerry and I washed every single glass.
Good old Marcello! Together with his willing band of helpers, his hard work in organising another Sunday afternoon Italian ``binge'' at the Hall netted the Club nigh on £200.
On they came: the veterans, the faster ladies, the younger men, until Marco and Marcello brought up what would normally have been the back of the field, penalised by well over 10 minutes.

Marcello cooked the meal, the waitresses were Belgrave girls and it seemed that at least half the diners were from our Club. When it came to the raffle no fewer than nine of the ten prizes went to Belgravians.
Marcello pulled a calf muscle in the 5000m and a sick Steve Halliday doubled up in the 1500 and 5000m but it all proved too much and we drifted to 3rd but retained overall 2nd place in the league.
Once again Marcello did the catering - how does that man cook for so many on such primitive equipment? They're lining up another one for some time in the Spring so keep your eyes open for details.
I want to invite you to Italy for races (I am investigating the possibilities!). Marcello knows my address.
We lost a few marks when the 'chase was cancelled due to the groundsman having failed to fill the water jump; poor old Marcello had made every effort to arrive early for it was well.
Conditions were so slippery that most had trouble keeping their feet at some stage but Marcello seemed to suffer the most, looking as if he'd be much happier wearing a pair of skis.
Marcello had been suffering from a groin strain in the weeks before and had been a doubtful starter. He gamely plugged away but we were down to 14th with a quarter of the race gone.
Marcello, too, had his pride at stake and although Ray was just two seconds outside his own record, he gained no more than that on the 'A' team.
